answer.rationale: The primary supply contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so a decision is forced. Finance mandates an 18% cut to component spend. Memory c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate — this is the most directly relevant precedent for achieving the cost cut within the 14-day window. Memory c1 (renew incumbent) kept integration stable but at the incumbent's pricing, which likely cannot meet the 18% reduction without a separate negotiation action (memory c4), and we only get one action this cycle. Memory c3 (add second source) addresses single-point-of-failure risk but does not itself reduce cost. Deferring (memory c5) is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew and the line is already at 94% with no buffer — a lapse would immediately threaten delivery. I am pulling memory c2's archived record to confirm the onboarding speed is compatible with the 14-day window and that the cost reduction was on components comparable to our current primary supply. If the archive confirms fast onboarding and accurate invoicing, I will execute switch_primary_vendor. If it reveals hidden costs or a longer integration tail than the summary suggests, I will fall back to negotiate_terms with the incumbent to hit as much of the 18% target as possible while preserving delivery continuity.
